rationale: A wins because it finds the third real story in the update instead of padding the same company-growth idea twice: "Anker says its home battery skips the rewiring — installers will decide if that's true" is the beat-level stress test a trade reporter can actually report. B's "The power-bank company just built a whole-home battery" and "Why a phone-charger giant is betting on home energy storage" are two wrappers on the same angle, and it also says "Anker naming Tesla Powerwall as direct competition," which the update did not say. A still has a little launch-day swagger, but it owns the holes instead of decorating them.
gaps_in_A: "a purchase measured in thousands of dollars and decades on the wall" stretches beyond the supplied facts; pricing is only partially disclosed and warranty terms are not detailed.

"The widely held position on this beat is that whole-home storage means electricians, panel work, and permitting" is plausible beat context, but it is not in the update; frame it as a hypothesis for installers to test.
The refused "A profitable public company takes on Tesla's cash-hungry energy business" should be killed for invented financial characterization too, not only as a duplicate.
gaps_in_B: "Anker naming Tesla Powerwall as direct competition" invents attribution. The update says it competes with Tesla Powerwall; it does not say Anker named or explicitly positioned against Tesla.

"The power-bank company just built a whole-home battery" and "Why a phone-charger giant is betting on home energy storage" are too close; brand trust and corporate diversification are not enough separation to count as two clean angles here.
It buries the strongest technical story, "installs without major electrical rewiring," inside proof instead of making installers/electricians the protagonist.
"funding-style strategy analysis" and "deploying capital" dress the angle in finance clothing without supplied investment size, target revenue, or capital-allocation detail.
